sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Acute dacryocystitis is an infection of the lacrimal sac, usually secondary to obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct (NLD). Stasis of tears leads to bacterial overgrowth and subsequent inflammation, which can progress to abscess formation or orbital cellulitis.

rows: Staph. aureus, Strep. pneumoniae, H. influenzae
Strep. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Staph. aureus

sections.title: Clinical Signs & Symptoms
content: Painful, erythematous swelling over the medial canthal area (lacrimal sac region).
Epiphora (overflow tearing) due to NLD obstruction.
Purulent discharge expressed through the punctum (diagnostic maneuver).
Tenderness, warmth, and induration of the surrounding periocular tissues.
Potential for pre-septal cellulitis or frank abscess formation.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Warm compresses to localize infection.
Step 2: Systemic antibiotics (e.g., Augmentin 875/125mg BID or Cephalexin).
Step 3: Incision and Drainage (I&D) IF fluctuation/abscess is present.
Step 4: Irrigation of the lacrimal system is CONTRAINDICATED during acute phase.
Step 5: Definitive Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) performed after inflammation resolves.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Admit
content: Signs of Orbital Cellulitis: Ophthalmoplegia, proptosis, vision loss, or relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD).
Systemic sepsis: Fever > 38.5°C, altered mental status, tachycardia.
Extension of inflammation beyond the medial canthal area.
Failure to respond to outpatient oral antibiotics within 48 hours.

content.explanation: L: Lacrimal sac swelling, A: Acute pain, C: Chronic epiphora, R: Redness, I: Infection (purulence), M: Medial location, A: Antibiotics needed, L: Likely NLD obstruction.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Do NOT probe or syringe the system during the acute phase (risk of sepsis spreading).
If recurrence occurs, suspect lacrimal sac malignancy (biopsy mandatory).
Always evaluate for concomitant sinusitis on clinical exam.
Augmentin is the drug of choice due to high beta-lactamase resistance.
